lead: A reference project on the language of sulfur chemistry: German and English terms, the compounds they name, and the evidence behind each statement.

sections.heading: Start with a governed reference
paragraphs: {{GOV:knowledge_objects}} reference records have been built under the current rules so far. The first covers molybdenum disulfide (MoS2): its formula, its layered bulk structure, the 1T, 2H and 3R polytypes, and two independent determinations of the 2H lattice parameter. It rests on {{GOV:mos2_admitted_evidence}} admitted evidence records, each traced to the study or database that produced it.

sections.heading: The question in our name
paragraphs: 'Bisulfid' and 'bisulfide' differ by one letter. Whether 'Bisulfid' is simply the German spelling of the English term is itself a terminology claim, and it is handled like any other claim on this site: it will be stated as fact only after its sources are verified and admitted.

The terminology record sets out, from {{GOV:term_evidence}} admitted evidence records and {{GOV:term_claims_approved}} reviewed claims, which meaning dictionaries, IUPAC and a chemical database attach to each spelling, and where the evidence stops. {{GOV:bisulfid_claims_pending}} related claims remain open.

sections.heading: How a statement reaches a reference page
paragraphs: A source is first identified and checked, then qualified for a specific use. A passage from it is recorded as evidence with its exact location, and a claim is approved only against admitted evidence. Numbers are quoted as their sources print them; when two determinations differ, both are shown rather than averaged. A new reference page is published only if it adds knowledge that no other page on the site already holds; most older pages were published before these rules and are being reviewed or rebuilt.

sections.heading: English and German
paragraphs: The site is maintained in English and German. A German page exists when it answers a German-language question, such as which form a German technical text uses, rather than as a copy of an English page.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for this site
paragraphs: BISULFID is an independent reference project published by the owner of the bisulfid.com domain. It is not affiliated with IUPAC, with any dictionary publisher or with any company or database named on its pages.

Each reference page built under these rules names the evidence behind every statement and shows when it was retrieved. No individual expert review is claimed: a page records that it has been independently validated only after such a review has taken place.

sections.heading: What you will not find here
paragraphs: BISULFID does not give safety, handling, medical, procurement or investment guidance. For those, use the safety data sheet of the specific product and a qualified professional.
